note: Read 2026-11-01 at the owner's word ("Build those first 3 starting with ledger first"; of the 21 countries read first: "It should cover across every country"; "Retry the blocked tax facts once all countries land"): the tax on a screen worker's pay in Tanzania: a resident's income tax, social contributions, what is withheld at source, a non-resident artiste's withholding, an author's treatment, VAT and the tax year. figures.finding: A Tanzanian resident pays income tax by a monthly scale: nothing on income to TZS 270,000 a month, then 8%, 20%, 25%, and 30% above TZS 1,000,000.
figures.applies: 2026, Tanzania Mainland and Zanzibar alike. Annual bands are the monthly ones times twelve.

sources.said: For Tanzania Mainland Monthly Taxable Income Tax Rate Where total Income does not exceed Tshs. 270,000/= NIL Where the total Income exceeds Tshs. 270,000/= but does not exceed Tshs. 520,000/= 8% of the amount in excess of the amount in excess of Tshs. 270,000/= Where total Income exceeds Tshs. 520,000/= but does not exceed Tshs. 760,000/= Tshs. 20,000/= plus 20% of the amount in excess of Tshs. 520,000/= Where total Income exceeds Tshs. 760,000/= but does not exceed Tshs. 1,000,000/= Tshs. 68,000/= plus 25% of the amount in excess of Tshs. 760,000/= Where total Income exceeds Tshs. 1,000,000/= Tshs. 128,000/= plus 30% of the amount in excess of Tshs. 1,000,000/= Note: Threshold per annum : Annual Income of Tshs 3,240,000/= is not taxable … For Zanzibar Monthly Taxable Income Tax Rate Where total Income does not exceed Tshs. 270,000/= NIL

figures.finding: The private-sector employer pays 20% of remuneration to the National Social Security Fund and may recover up to half (10%) from the employee; the employer also pays a 3.5% skills levy (10 or more employees) and 0.5% workers' compensation.

sources.said: The employer’s contribution is 20% of the employee’s remuneration; however, the employer is entitled to recover up to half of this from the employee.
SDL is a tax on the employer calculated as 3.5% of gross cash emoluments of employees.
calculated as a percentage of cash sums paid to employees at 0.5%.

figures.finding: Employment income is taxed by PAYE withheld by the employer; service fees paid to a resident bear 5% withholding and royalties 15% (10% for film, video or sound recordings).

sources.said: Tax on employment income is accounted for by the employer WHT at source under the pay-as-you-earn (PAYE) scheme.
Service fees 5 15
If payment relates to use of cinematography film, video tape sound recording, or any other like medium, the applicable rate is 10%.

figures.finding: A non-resident pays a final flat 15% on employment income from Tanzania, and 15% withholding on service fees and royalties; personal services have a Tanzanian source where performed in Tanzania.

sources.said: Non-resident individuals are subject to tax at a flat rate of 15% on employment income, which is final tax in Tanzania.
Personal services have a Tanzanian source if (i) performed in Tanzania or (ii) performed outside Tanzania but where the payer is the government of Tanzania.
Royalty* 15 15

figures.finding: VAT is 18% on the mainland (15% in Zanzibar); registration is required at TZS 200 million of taxable turnover, or for designated services whatever the turnover.

sources.said: The standard rate of VAT is 18%
reaching a TZS 200 million threshold of turnover from taxable supplies; (ii) providing designated services, irrespective of turnover

figures.finding: The tax year is the calendar year; a person with income beyond employment files an estimate by 31 March, pays quarterly instalments, and files the final return within six months of the year's end.

sources.said: The tax year runs from 1 January to 31 December.
A final tax return contains a statement of chargeable income for the year of income and is due for filing within six months of the end of the year of income.
Any final tax payable is due by the deadline for filing the final tax return.
